newsitem.title: SAUDI ARABIA: Saudi minister evades question on ties with Iran.
newsitem.headline: Saudi minister evades question on ties with Iran.

text.p: Saudi Arabia's Defence Minister Prince Sultan said Riyadh wanted good relations with other states, evading a question on comments by Iran' foreign minister that a new chapter has opened between the two countries.
"We look forward to good relations with every person who wants (common) good, love and harmony," Prince Sultan said.
The official Saudi Press Agency said Prince Sultan made his comment late on Saturday when asked by journalists about the remarks by Iran's Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati.
Velayati said on Friday that his tour in the past week of six Gulf Arab states opened a new chapter in often tense ties between Iran and its Arab neighbours across the Gulf.
He said his talks with Saudi King Fahd, Crown Prince Abdullah and Foreign Minister Prince Saud al-Faisal could "serve as a turning point in Tehran-Riyadh relations".
Iran's relations with its Gulf Arab neighbours are often tense. Gulf Arab states have accused Iran of interfering in their internal affairs, a charge Iran denies.
Riyadh has refused to confirm U.S. media reports of an Iranian link to a bomb attack that killed 19 U.S. servicemen in the eastern Saudi city of Khobar last June.
Iran -- which Washington has accused of sponsoring state terrorism and has imposed sanctions on -- denies any role.
